order.step: ePTFE plug through the right wall
order.note: from outside, through the 12.6 mm hole

order.step: ePTFE nut, lowered in from above
order.note: The cavity is open until the lid goes on. The nut drops straight onto the thread.

order.step: ePTFE nut, slid on along the axis instead
order.note: Closed path. The 16 mm nut passes the battery pocket rib at x 57.5 to 59. The rib ends at z 12. The vent axis is at z 13.
fit it before the battery plate

order.step: LiPo 103450 into the pocket, the other option
order.note: This is the alternative to the adapter with the 852040. Do not fit both.

order.step: battery plate onto the pocket walls
PCB down onto the pillars, 0.6 forward for the lips
order.note: The board is 47 mm long in a 47.8 mm slot. It starts forward of its seat.

order.step: PCB slid back 0.6 under the hold-down lips
order.note: A horizontal slide at board height. The board top is at 17.3 mm. The underside of the lip is at 17.8 mm.

order.step: lid onto the base, skirt into the cavity
M3x40 x4 from below, into the inserts
order.note: The 2.7 mm captive neck is a press fit by design. The tool relieves it here, as the check() in the macro does

order.step: leg 1 tongue into the Y tunnel, pushed -Y
order.note: Push the leg in from the +Y side. The tongue, web and heel cross the tunnel. The barbs deflect 1.4 mm on each side. The wall pad, plate and foot stay at y >= 54.6 mm, outside the box.

order.step: leg 1 tongue into the Y tunnel, pushed +Y
order.note: Closed path. The wall pad leads and must cross the 4.6 mm end walls

order.step: tray 1 channel onto the heel rail
leg 2 tongue into the Y tunnel, pushed -Y
tray 2 channel onto the heel rail

skipped.components onto the PCB: The components are soldered on before the board goes in. The PCB step carries the envelope
skipped.U.FL pigtail onto the PCB socket: The pigtail is flexible and has no rigid insertion path. The static keep-out check in the macro covers it
skipped.O-ring cord into the groove: The cord is flexible and is pressed in. The groove depth is the design rule that applies
skipped.solar panel leads into the feedthrough: The leads are flexible and are potted after the lid is on. The macro checks the bore, the potting cup and the wire path
skipped.pegs and cable ties through the eyelets: They are flexible. They go in last and block no step
